mainTopic: Who is the תנא of the משנה on a גוי's versus a ישראל's חמץ after פסח, and the ברייתא of מעילה with consecrated חמץ that led רב אחא בר יעקב to retract
overview: The משנה rules that חמץ owned by a גוי during פסח is permitted for benefit afterward, while a ישראל's חמץ is forbidden. The גמרא asks which תנא this fits, since רבי יהודה, רבי שמעון and רבי יוסי הגלילי each seem not to match. רב אחא בר יעקב says it is רבי יהודה, who learns from the word שאור that the eating ban, like בל יראה, covers only your own חמץ. He explains that the משנה's narrow wording just mirrors the ישראל clause. רבא says it is רבי שמעון, and that the ban on a ישראל's חמץ is a rabbinic קנס for violating בל יראה and בל ימצא. The verse the משנה quotes seems to fit only רבא, but the גמרא shows it also fits רב אחא בר יעקב, because the verse explains the first clause. The two אמוראים are consistent with their dispute about whether one who eats a גוי's שאור after פסח gets מלקות according to רבי יהודה. רב אחא בר יעקב later retracted because of a ברייתא about eating חמץ של הקדש during פסח, which רבי יוחנן and רב יוסף each explain in their own way. The amud ends as רב אחא בר רבא's version of the teaching begins; it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה Fits Neither רבי שמעון Nor רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: Continuing its search for the משנה's author, the גמרא shows that רבי שמעון would permit even a ישראל's חמץ, and רבי יוסי הגלילי would permit benefit even during פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: [If the משנה follows רבי שמעון], he permits even a ישראל's חמץ! And if it follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, he permits benefit from חמץ even during פסח itself!
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the middle of a question. The גמרא is finishing its list of why no known תנא fits the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה has two parts: a גוי's חמץ is permitted after פסח, and a ישראל's is forbidden. רבי שמעון would permit both, so he contradicts the second part. רבי יוסי הגלילי allows benefit even during פסח, so the משנה's stress on 'after פסח' would make no sense for him.

keyTerms.meaning: He actually permits it
During its time, meaning during פסח
Benefit, such as selling it or feeding it to animals, as opposed to eating
A תנא who holds that חמץ is forbidden only for eating, not for benefit, even during פסח

steps.confusionAlert: The first words, 'even a Jew's he permits', are the end of the clause about רבי שמעון. His name appeared on the previous amud.

phrases.english: [If it is Rabbi Shimon] — even a Jew's [chametz] he permits!
phrases.notes: Ends the רבי שמעון clause that began on the previous amud

phrases.english: And if it is Rabbi Yosei HaGelili —
even during its time [Pesach]
he also permits it for benefit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the 'who is the תנא' question that began on the previous amud
steps.kashyaTarget: The attempt to attribute the משנה to רבי שמעון or רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each of these תנאים' known rulings contradicts one detail of the משנה

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב: It Is רבי יהודה, Using a Comparison of the Word שאור
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב says the משנה follows רבי יהודה. He learns that the eating prohibition, like the seeing prohibition, covers only your own חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: Really, it is רבי יהודה. He learns 'שאור' of eating from 'שאור' of seeing. With seeing, you may not see your own, but you may see that of others and that of הקדש. So too with eating: you may not eat your own, but you may eat that of others and that of הקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה can follow רבי יהודה after all. He does not forbid a גוי's חמץ, because he compares the eating verse to the seeing verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that רבי יהודה forbids חמץ after פסח, so he should forbid a גוי's too. רב אחא says רבי יהודה links the word שאור in the eating verse to שאור in the seeing verse. The seeing verse (בל יראה) is limited to 'yours', so the eating prohibition is limited to 'yours' as well. A גוי's חמץ and הקדש's חמץ are therefore excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually, used to defend an option that was just rejected
And he learns / derives
Leaven (sourdough starter), a word in both the eating and the seeing verses
Seeing, referring to the prohibition בל יראה
Belonging to On High, meaning הקדש (consecrated property)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the 'yours' limitation of בל יראה can carry over to other חמץ prohibitions. This becomes the basis for treating a גוי's חמץ differently.

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
Really, it is Rabbi Yehuda,
and he derives 'se'or' of eating
from 'se'or' of seeing.
Just as with 'se'or' of seeing —
your own you may not see,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אַתָּה רוֹאֶה שֶׁל אֲחֵרִים וְשֶׁל גָּבוֹהַּ.
phrases.english: but you may see that of others and that of the Most High (Temple property).
so too 'se'or' of eating —
your own you may not eat,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אַתָּה אוֹכֵל שֶׁל אֲחֵרִים וְשֶׁל גָּבוֹהַּ.
phrases.english: but you may eat that of others and that of the Most High.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'who is the תנא' difficulty by reviving רבי יהודה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Scriptural derivation that limits the prohibition (גזירה שוה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה forbids all חמץ after פסח, including a גוי's
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה forbids only a ישראל's own חמץ, learned from בל יראה

steps.title: Why the משנה Says Only 'Benefit' and Not 'Eating'
steps.stepSummary: By this approach, a גוי's חמץ could even be eaten. The משנה said 'benefit' only to match the wording of the ישראל clause.
steps.simpleTranslation: By right, the משנה should have taught that a גוי's חמץ is permitted even for eating. But since it taught that a ישראל's is forbidden for benefit, it also taught that a גוי's is permitted for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא handles a follow-up problem with רב אחא's answer. It explains why the משנה's wording seems too limited.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a גוי's חמץ is outside the eating prohibition entirely, it should be permitted even to eat. The משנה only says 'permitted for benefit' to keep it parallel with 'a ישראל's is forbidden for benefit'. So the wording is about style, not a limit on the law.

keyTerms.meaning: And by right / properly
That it should have taught
Since it taught, a formula for wording chosen to match a nearby clause
Eating

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the משנה's word 'benefit' as implying that eating is forbidden. According to רב אחא, eating a גוי's חמץ after פסח is permitted too.

phrases.english: And by right it should have taught
that even eating is also permitted,
but since it taught
that a Jew's is forbidden for benefit —
it also taught that a gentile's is permitted for benefit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב אחא's answer against an implied wording problem
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's 'benefit' suggests eating a גוי's חמץ is forbidden
steps.terutzMaskana: Eating is permitted as well; 'benefit' only mirrors the ישראל clause

steps.title: Why the משנה Says 'After פסח' and Not 'During'
steps.stepSummary: Likewise, a גוי's חמץ would be permitted for benefit even during פסח. The משנה said 'after its time' only to match the ישראל clause.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by right it should have taught that even during its time a גוי's חמץ is permitted for benefit. But since it taught about a ישראל's חמץ after its time, it also taught about a גוי's after its time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the same 'matching wording' idea to the time detail in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this approach, a גוי's חמץ is not 'yours', so a ישראל could benefit from it even during פסח. The משנה mentions only 'after פסח' because the ישראל clause is about after פסח. The two clauses were phrased in parallel.

keyTerms.meaning: After its time, meaning after פסח
A non-Jew

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אחא, the משנה follows רבי יהודה. A גוי's חמץ is fully permitted, even to eat and even during פסח. The משנה's narrower wording just mirrors the ישראל clause.

phrases.english: And by right it should have taught
that even during its time it is permitted for benefit,
but since it taught a Jew's case after its time —
it also taught the gentile's case after its time.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְדִין הוּא דְּאִיבְּעִי לֵיהּ לְמִיתְנֵא דַּאֲפִילּוּ בְּתוֹךְ זְמַנּוֹ מוּתָּר בַּהֲנָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same parallelism argument to the time detail
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase 'after פסח' implies a גוי's חמץ is forbidden during פסח
steps.terutzMaskana: It is permitted during פסח too; 'after' only mirrors the ישראל clause

steps.title: רבא: It Is רבי שמעון, With a Rabbinic Penalty
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the משנה follows רבי שמעון. The ban on a ישראל's חמץ after פסח is a קנס, a penalty for having violated בל יראה and בל ימצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Really, it is רבי שמעון. And רבי שמעון imposes a penalty, since the Jew transgressed בל יראה and בל ימצא with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a different answer to the original question. He revives רבי שמעון and explains the ban on a ישראל's חמץ as a penalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem with רבי שמעון was that he permits a ישראל's חמץ after פסח. רבא says that by Torah law he does permit it. However, the חכמים penalized the owner for keeping חמץ during פסח, so they forbade benefit from it. The core category stays permitted מדאורייתא; the ban is an added rabbinic consequence.

keyTerms.meaning: He imposes a penalty (rabbinic קנס)
Since / because
The prohibition 'it shall not be seen'
The prohibition 'it shall not be found'
A leading אמורא who offers a competing answer here

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers. רב אחא says the משנה is רבי יהודה, with a גזירה שוה limiting the prohibition to 'yours'. רבא says it is רבי שמעון, and the ban on a ישראל's חמץ is only a rabbinic קנס.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבא's answer is the source for חמץ שעבר עליו הפסח being forbidden as a rabbinic penalty, which is how the halacha is generally understood.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Really, it is Rabbi Shimon.
And Rabbi Shimon imposes a penalty,
since he transgressed with it
the prohibitions 'it shall not be seen' and 'it shall not be found.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב אחא's approach and answers the original question differently
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing Torah law from a rabbinic penalty
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון permits a ישראל's חמץ after פסח, so he cannot be the משנה's author
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון permits it מדאורייתא, but the חכמים penalized the owner, so it is forbidden for benefit

steps.title: Why does the משנה quote 'It shall not be seen' according to רב אחא בר יעקב?
steps.stepSummary: The verse 'לא יראה' fits רבא well. According to רב אחא בר יעקב, though, the משנה should have quoted 'לא יאכל חמץ'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to רבא, this explains what the משנה teaches: a ישראל's חמץ is forbidden because the תורה says 'It shall not be seen.' But according to רב אחא בר יעקב, the משנה should have said 'because of: לא יאכל חמץ'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks both explanations against the verse the משנה actually quotes. That verse fits רבא, but it seems to clash with רב אחא בר יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the ban on a ישראל's חמץ after פסח is a קנס for breaking 'לא יראה', so quoting that verse makes sense. For רב אחא בר יעקב, the ban comes from רבי יהודה's reading of the eating verse. So the משנה seems to have quoted the wrong verse.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / this works well for one side (opens a challenge to the other side)
'It shall not be seen': the Torah's ban on having חמץ seen during פסח
'Chametz shall not be eaten': the Torah's ban on eating חמץ
It should have said

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rava,
this explains what is taught:
that of a Jew is forbidden,
because it is said: "It shall not be seen."
But according to Rav Acha bar Yaakov,
it should have said: because of "Chametz shall not be eaten"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two explanations from steps 2 and 5 against the verse the משנה quotes.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בר יעקב's claim that the משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ban on a ישראל's חמץ comes from the eating verse, the משנה would cite that verse, not 'לא יראה'.

steps.title: The verse supports the first clause, about a גוי's חמץ
steps.stepSummary: The proof-verse goes on the first clause. 'לא יראה לך' shows that only your own חמץ is forbidden, so a גוי's חמץ is permitted. רבי יהודה applies the same limit to the eating ban.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think the verse goes on the last clause? It goes on the first clause, and this is what the משנה means: a גוי's חמץ that stayed through פסח is permitted for benefit, because the Torah says 'It shall not be seen by you.' You may not see your own, but you may see that of others and that of the הקדש. And רבי יהודה learns the eating ban on שאור from the seeing ban on שאור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אחא בר יעקב. The verse 'לא יראה' is not the source of the ban on a ישראל's חמץ. It is the reason a גוי's חמץ is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'לך' (to you) limits בל יראה to your own חמץ. רבי יהודה copies that limit over to the eating ban, so a גוי's חמץ is not forbidden at all. That is why the משנה quotes the seeing verse even according to רב אחא בר יעקב.

keyTerms.meaning: It refers to the last clause
It refers to the first clause
Belonging to 'the One Above', i.e., הקדש
Sourdough / leavening agent
He learns / derives (one law from another)

steps.confusionAlert: The verse 'לא יראה לך' is quoted here to permit (a גוי's חמץ), not to forbid. Do not read it as the source of the ישראל's ban in רב אחא בר יעקב's view.

phrases.english: Do you think it refers to the last clause?!
It refers to the first clause,
and this is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: חָמֵץ שֶׁל גּוֹי שֶׁעָבַר עָלָיו הַפֶּסַח
phrases.english: Chametz of a gentile that remained through Pesach
is permitted for benefit,
because it is said: "It shall not be seen by you".
Your own you may not see,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אַתָּה רוֹאֶה שֶׁל אֲחֵרִים וְשֶׁל גָּבוֹהַּ.
phrases.english: but you may see that of others and that of Heaven (hekdesh).
And he derives leaven of eating from leaven of seeing.
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה applies the 'yours only' limit of seeing to eating.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading which clause of the משנה the verse belongs to
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse was the source for forbidding a ישראל's חמץ (the last clause).
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse explains why a גוי's חמץ is permitted (the first clause), through 'לך' and the link between eating and seeing.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אחא בר יעקב, 'לא יראה לך' is quoted to permit a גוי's חמץ. רבי יהודה links the eating ban to the seeing ban.

steps.title: רבא and רב אחא בר יעקב argue the same way elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: The same two אמוראים argue about whether one who eats a גוי's שאור after פסח gets מלקות according to רבי יהודה. רבא says yes and רב אחא בר יעקב says no.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they follow their own reasoning. For it was stated: someone eats a גוי's שאור that stayed through פסח. According to רבי יהודה, רבא says he gets lashes, and רב אחא בר יעקב says he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבא and רב אחא בר יעקב hold these same positions in a separate, recorded dispute. This sets up the next step, which explains each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a גוי's חמץ eaten after פסח, according to רבי יהודה, who holds that חמץ after its time is forbidden by Torah law. If the eating ban covers even a גוי's חמץ, the eater is flogged. If it covers only a ישראל's חמץ, he is not.

keyTerms.meaning: They follow their own line of reasoning
For it was stated (introduces an אמוראים dispute)
He receives lashes (מלקות) for breaking a Torah prohibition

phrases.english: And they follow their own reasoning:
for it was stated:
One who eats leaven of a gentile
that remained through Pesach,
according to the words of Rabbi Yehuda:
Rava said: he is flogged,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר: אֵינוֹ לוֹקֶה.
phrases.english: and Rav Acha bar Yaakov said: he is not flogged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the positions of steps 2, 5 and 7 match a separate dispute between the same אמוראים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, רבא says one who eats a גוי's שאור after פסח is flogged; רב אחא בר יעקב says he is not.

steps.title: Each side's reasoning: does רבי יהודה link eating to seeing?
steps.stepSummary: רבא holds that רבי יהודה does not learn the eating ban from the seeing ban, so even a גוי's חמץ is forbidden. רב אחא בר יעקב holds that he does, so only your own חמץ is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says he is flogged, because רבי יהודה does not learn the eating ban on שאור from the seeing ban on שאור. רב אחא בר יעקב says he is not flogged, because רבי יהודה does learn the eating ban from the seeing ban.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind each side of the dispute. It all depends on one question: does רבי יהודה copy the 'yours only' limit from seeing over to eating?
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the eating ban has no 'לך' limit, so any חמץ is included, even a גוי's, and the eater gets מלקות. For רב אחא בר יעקב, eating is limited like seeing, so a גוי's חמץ is not included and there are no מלקות. This is exactly what drove each one's explanation of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The eating ban on leaven
The seeing ban on leaven

steps.whatToRemember: The whole disagreement comes down to one point. רב אחא בר יעקב says רבי יהודה links the eating ban to the seeing ban (only your own is forbidden). רבא says he does not (all חמץ is forbidden). That is why רבא needed רבי שמעון and a קנס to explain the משנה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that each אמורא's reading of the משנה matches a consistent view of how רבי יהודה reads the verses, and that view has a real result: whether מלקות is given.

phrases.english: Rava said: he is flogged,
because Rabbi Yehuda does not derive
leaven of eating from leaven of seeing.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר: אֵינוֹ לוֹקֶה,
phrases.english: And Rav Acha bar Yaakov said: he is not flogged,
because he derives leaven of eating from leaven of seeing.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: לוֹקֶה, לָא יָלֵיף רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind each side of the dispute quoted in step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The dispute between רבא and רב אחא בר יעקב depends on whether רבי יהודה links the eating ban to the seeing ban. That decides both how each explains the משנה and whether the eater gets מלקות.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב retracts, based on a ברייתא about consecrated חמץ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that רב אחא בר יעקב retracted his earlier position. It cites a ברייתא as the reason: one who eats חמץ של הקדש during פסח is guilty of מעילה, while 'יש אומרים' say he is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב took back that opinion. This is because a ברייתא teaches: Someone who eats consecrated חמץ during פסח has committed מעילה (misuse of holy property). Some say: he has not committed מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says רב אחא בר יעקב changed his mind about his earlier view. It brings a ברייתא that pushed him to retract.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, רב אחא בר יעקב held that the משנה follows רבי יהודה, who forbids חמץ after פסח from the Torah. מעילה only applies to something with monetary value, so the first opinion in the ברייתא assumes חמץ is worth something. The coming steps explain it two ways. According to רבי יוחנן, this points to רבי שמעון, who permits benefit from חמץ after פסח, which is רבא's view. According to רב יוסף, both sides follow רבי יוסי הגלילי. Either way, the ברייתא does not fit רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: He retracted (changed his mind)
חמץ that was consecrated to the בית המקדש
He committed מעילה, misuse of holy property. It requires a קרבן אשם and repayment, and applies only to things with monetary value.
During the festival, here meaning during פסח
'Some say', an unnamed dissenting opinion

steps.whyThisMatters: If רב אחא בר יעקב retracts, the dispute between him and רבא falls away. Everyone would then explain the משנה like רבא, as following רבי שמעון.

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲדַר בֵּיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב מֵהַהִיא,
phrases.english: And Rav Acha bar Yaakov retracted from that position,
phrases.notes: 'That' refers to his view that the משנה follows רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: as it was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: הָאוֹכֵל חָמֵץ שֶׁל הֶקְדֵּשׁ בַּמּוֹעֵד — מָעַל.
phrases.english: One who eats consecrated chametz during the festival has committed me'ilah.
phrases.notes: Me'ilah requires the item to have monetary value.

phrases.english: And some say: he has not committed me'ilah.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲדַר בֵּיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב מֵהַהִיא, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the dispute between רבא and רב אחא בר יעקב by reporting that רב אחא בר יעקב retracted.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה follows רבי שמעון, so חמץ after פסח has value, against רב אחא בר יעקב's earlier view
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about eating חמץ של הקדש during פסח

steps.title: Who is the 'some say' opinion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the anonymous 'יש אומרים' in the ברייתא is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the one called 'some say'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question: which תנא holds the 'יש אומרים' view? This sets up the next step, where the answer explains how the ברייתא proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We need to know why the 'יש אומרים' exempts the eater from מעילה. If the reason is that חמץ has no value, the proof fails. If the reason is something else, both sides agree חמץ has value.

keyTerms.meaning: Who?

phrases.english: Who is 'some say'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the identity of the dissenting opinion in the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity, and so the reasoning, of the 'יש אומרים' who says לא מעל

steps.title: רבי יוחנן identifies the opinion as רבי נחוניא בן הקנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the 'יש אומרים' is רבי נחוניא בן הקנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: It is רבי נחוניא בן הקנה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question by naming the תנא behind 'יש אומרים'. The next step brings a ברייתא showing what this תנא holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Naming רבי נחוניא בן הקנה tells us his reason for exempting the eater. It is not that חמץ is worthless. It is his rule that someone facing a death-level punishment does not also pay.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא with a known view on penalties for יום הכפורים

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
It is Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKana.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: רַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא בֶּן הַקָּנָה הִיא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'יש אומרים' is רבי נחוניא בן הקנה

steps.title: רבי נחוניא treats יום הכפורים like שבת for exemption from payment
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי נחוניא בן הקנה compares יום הכפורים to שבת. Whoever is liable for a death-level punishment is exempt from paying. So for him, the כרת for eating חמץ cancels the מעילה payment, not any lack of value.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי נחוניא בן הקנה would treat יום הכפורים like שבת regarding payments. Just as on שבת a person is liable with his life and is exempt from payment, so too on יום הכפורים a person is liable with his life and is exempt from payment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show רבי נחוניא בן הקנה's rule. When one act carries both a death-level punishment and a payment, he is exempt from paying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת, causing damage through a forbidden act brings סקילה, so there is no payment (קים ליה בדרבה מיניה). רבי נחוניא extends this to יום הכפורים, which carries כרת, and so also to eating חמץ on פסח, which also carries כרת. His 'לא מעל' therefore means 'exempt because of כרת', so both sides agree חמץ has value, which fits רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: Payments or monetary compensation
Liable with his life, meaning a death penalty or כרת
Exempt
Like שבת

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'לא מעל' as saying the חמץ is worthless. According to רבי יוחנן, the 'יש אומרים' agrees it has value. He exempts the eater only because the bigger punishment, כרת, cancels the payment.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, both opinions in the ברייתא assume consecrated חמץ has value. That fits רבי שמעון, who permits benefit from חמץ after פסח, and this is why רב אחא בר יעקב retracted.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKana
would treat Yom Kippur
like Shabbat with regard to payments.
Just as on Shabbat one is liable with his life
and is exempt from payment,
so too on Yom Kippur one is liable with his life
and is exempt from payment.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא בֶּן הַקָּנָה הָיָה עוֹשֶׂה אֶת יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים כַּשַּׁבָּת לְתַשְׁלוּמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's identification by showing רבי נחוניא's known rule about exemption from payment.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי נחוניא בן הקנה exempts payment whenever a death-level punishment applies, which explains his 'לא מעל'
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא comparing יום הכפורים to שבת regarding payments

steps.title: רב יוסף: the dispute is about redeeming holy items to feed dogs
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף reads the ברייתא differently. Both sides follow רבי יוסי הגלילי, who permits benefit from חמץ during פסח. They argue about whether קדשים may be redeemed to feed them to dogs. On this reading the ברייתא is no proof for רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: They disagree about whether one may redeem consecrated items in order to feed them to dogs.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף offers a different explanation of the ברייתא. This removes its force as proof that both sides agree with רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Consecrated חמץ during פסח has one possible use: feeding it to dogs. The first opinion holds that one may redeem קדשים for dog food, so the חמץ has value and the eater is guilty of מעילה. The 'יש אומרים' holds that one may not, so it has no value and there is no מעילה. Neither side needs רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: Redeeming consecrated items, so their holiness transfers to money
To feed them to dogs
They disagree about

steps.whyThisMatters: רב יוסף disagrees with רבי יוחנן only about why the 'יש אומרים' exempts the eater from מעילה. On his reading, both opinions in the ברייתא still hold that חמץ may be used for benefit, like רבי יוסי הגלילי, so neither follows רבי יהודה. The ברייתא therefore still does not fit רב אחא בר יעקב's original reading of רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Regarding whether one may redeem consecrated items
in order to feed them to dogs, they disagree.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: בְּפוֹדִין אֶת הַקֳּדָשִׁים לְהַאֲכִילָן לִכְלָבִים קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation of the ברייתא than רבי יוחנן's, removing its proof for רבי שמעון.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference that both opinions in the ברייתא must follow רבי שמעון
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can follow רבי יוסי הגלילי, with the dispute being about redeeming קדשים to feed dogs rather than about payment versus כרת

steps.title: Each side of the ברייתא explained by redeeming קדשים for dogs
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף spells out his reading. The one who says מעל holds that we may redeem קדשים to feed them to dogs. The one who says לא מעל holds that we may not redeem them for that purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says he committed מעילה holds that we may redeem קדשים in order to feed them to dogs. The one who says he did not commit מעילה holds that we may not redeem them for that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב יוסף's new reading of the ברייתא. It tells us exactly what each side holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If קדשים may be redeemed for dog food, then the הקדש חמץ is still worth money during פסח, so eating it is מעילה. If they may not be redeemed for that, the חמץ is worth nothing, so there is no מעילה. Either way, the dispute is about redeeming קדשים, not about חמץ, so the ברייתא proves nothing for רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: He committed מעילה, meaning he used or ate הקדש property for himself
He holds (introduces the reasoning behind a position)
We redeem consecrated items, swapping their holiness onto money
To feed them to dogs
We do not redeem them for this purpose

steps.confusionAlert: This argument is not about whether חמץ is allowed for benefit. Both sides agree with רבי יוסי הגלילי that it is. The only argument is about redeeming קדשים for dog food.
steps.whyThisMatters: This completes רב יוסף's alternative to רבי יוחנן. Both sides accept that חמץ is permitted for benefit, as רבי יוסי הגלילי holds. Whether consecrated חמץ has value during פסח depends only on whether קדשים may be redeemed to feed dogs.

phrases.english: The one who said he committed misuse (of consecrated property)
holds: we may redeem consecrated items
in order to feed them to dogs.
phrases.notes: So the חמץ still has value, and eating it is מעילה.

phrases.english: And the one who said he did not commit misuse
holds: we may not redeem (for that purpose).
phrases.notes: So the חמץ has no value, and there is no מעילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב יוסף's rereading from step 14 by explaining the reasoning of each side.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי יוחנן's explanation that the 'יש אומרים' exempts only because of כרת, and so rejects reading the ברייתא as following רבי שמעון.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the dispute was about the value of חמץ. Actually it is about whether קדשים may be redeemed to feed dogs.

steps.title: רב אחא בר רבא's version is introduced
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to quote how רב אחא בר רבא taught this matter. His actual words continue on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר רבא taught it (in his own way).
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is getting ready to present רב אחא בר רבא's version of the teaching, which comes right on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תְּנָא לָהּ means he had his own way of teaching this material. The content of his version follows on the next amud. So here we only learn whose version is coming.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who presents his own version of the teaching
He taught it, introducing a version of a teaching

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא בַּר רָבָא תְּנָא לָהּ
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Rava taught it
phrases.notes: The content of his teaching continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר רָבָא תְּנָא לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב יוסף's reading, the גמרא turns to another version of the same teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces רב אחא בר רבא's version. The ruling itself comes on the next amud.
